sets.title: CPU budget: what costs the 68000 its frame
sets.intro: Your note 20261014-170114-5d29 (0.10.92, Moriya, stage 4 boss wave). Analysis only: nothing is changed in the game. Your run was replayed in our emulator with a cycle counter on every 68000 instruction (tools/brawler/cpu_profile.py). Numbers are % of one video frame (202,752 cycles). Full tables: docs/brawler_cpu_budget.md.

questions.title: Finding 1: frames are dropped, and the meter hides it
questions.context: 650 of 4196 frames dropped (15 %). With 6 enemies, 1 tick in 4 needs 2 frames: those fights run at about 80 % speed. The meter shows the worst tick of 16 that still fit; a tick that overruns shows only the idle left in its second frame, so it reads LOW. Per tick with 6 enemies: median 92 %, p90 109 %, p99 148 %. P1 alone: 60 %. Each enemy costs about 4 %. 57 % of the overruns happen while P1 is in a special.

media.caption: Every tick of your run. Above the dashed line = 2+ frames (a dropped frame). At 35 s the boss wave spawns: one tick of 4.3 frames.

questions.title: Finding 2: where the frame goes
questions.context: With 6 enemies: draw 25 % (sprite block writes, line guard, stage), fighters 14 %, HUD bars 10 % (every bar redrawn every tick), collision 10 %, AI 6 %, screen edges 5 %, depth sort 4 %, VRAM flush 3 %, BIOS 2 %. Spikes: the boss wave's spawn tints palettes colour by colour (a 70 ms freeze); with 6 effects on screen the line guard alone takes up to 33 %.

media.caption: Mean cost per subsystem: P1 alone / 6 enemies (fits) / 6 enemies (overruns)

questions.title: A. HUD bars: redraw a bar only when its value changes
questions.context: Saves ~9 % (bar_draw: 10 % mean, 23 % peak). Today every bar (2 lives, target, up to 8 drive chunks, boss) recomputes every cell every tick. Same picture. Risk low, effort small.

questions.title: B. Wave / boss spawn: tinted palettes precomputed
questions.context: Removes the 4-frame freeze (~70 ms) when a wave arrives: 6 enemies x their palettes x 15 colours, 6 multiplies per colour, all in one tick. Computed at build time (or once per fighter + colour set + tint). Risk low, effort small.

questions.title: C. Line guard: cache each entity's band span
questions.context: Removes the spikes: with 6 effects on screen the per-column band count costs up to 33 % of a frame (mean ~2 %). The span is recomputed only when the entity's frame changes. Risk medium (the per-line sprite limit must stay exact), effort medium.

questions.title: D. Sprite blocks: write Y / X only for blocks that changed
questions.context: Saves ~5 %. Today all 25 blocks' position words are rewritten and flushed every tick, moved or not (draw 6 + fighter_place 4.6 + VRAM flush 3.3). Risk medium (VRAM state must stay right), effort medium.

questions.title: E. Collision: active lists once per tick, strike only for live boxes
questions.context: Saves ~5 % (combat 6.6 + strike 3.2 at 6 enemies, 46 % peak). Today several passes over all 16 entities, and strike() is called for every attacker, mostly to return at once. Hit order must stay identical (regress traces). Risk medium, effort medium.

questions.title: F. AI: half the enemies think on even ticks, half on odd
questions.context: Saves ~3 % (ai_update 6 %, 9 % in overruns). Movement still every tick; decisions come 1 frame later. Risk: AI feel. Effort small.

questions.title: G. Small cleanups batch
questions.context: Saves ~6 %: the profiler's mark() still runs in normal builds (0.6), close_marks for players only (2.2 -> 0.5), depth sort on 16-bit keys of live entities (3.6 -> ~1), the second screen-edge pass only for fighters the combat moved, char_index cached. Risk low, effort small each.

questions.title: H. Meter: show dropped frames
questions.context: Today the meter shows the worst tick that fit, and overruns read low. Proposed: count the vblanks per tick and show e.g. CPU 140 % or the dropped frames per second. Risk none, effort small.

questions.title: I. 68000 asm for the remaining hot C loops (after A-G)
questions.context: About 2x on those loops (fighter_update state machine, collision pairs). Risk medium, effort high. Only worth it if A-G are not enough.

sets.title: Bonus game (T7): how to bring AOF's over
sets.intro: Art of Fighting 1 and 2 put a bonus game between fights. All clips come from our emulator (AOF1 / AOF2 ROMs, Ryo, default difficulty); they loop, tap to pause. Notes: /data/neogeo_dict/aof/bonus.md. Pick one answer per question; a note (type or speak) for anything else.

questions.title: The six AOF bonus games (for reference)
questions.context: When: AOF1 after every 2nd fight (3 times), AOF2 after every 3rd fight (3 times). A select screen offers 3 games, 9 s to choose. The reward only comes with the top grade. Life max = strength level x 8 and spirit max = spirit level x 8: levels start at 12 (96), each win +1 (+8), max 16 (128). AOF1 Bottle Cut: one press of A on a sweeping gauge, top 4 frames of 64 = all 5 bottles cut, spirit +1. AOF1 Ice Pillar: mash A for about 9 s, all pillars break = life +1. AOF1 Haoh Shoko-ken: do the super motion 6 times in about 30 s = the super works in fights from then on. AOF2 Spirit Training: one press on the gauge, Ryo punches the tree = spirit +1. AOF2 Strength Training: a real fight, knock down 10 thugs before the clock ends = life +1. AOF2 Super Death Blow: break 9 wooden posts with the super = super learned.

questions.context: A bonus stage becomes a level type in game.json (stages[] entry with "type": "bonus" and its fields), edited in the Factory Levels tab like the other levels; the engine reads the fields, nothing per fighter. Costs are my estimates; C ROM = the objects only (your fighter plays with his own sprites). Thug rush = AOF2 Strength Training with our enemies: clock + counter + tally. Break the objects = AOF2 posts / AOF1 ice as props that take hits and break, with your own moves. AOF1 pair = one press on a sweeping gauge (bottles) and mash A (ice), your fighter in front of the objects. All three = thug rush, gauge, posts broken with the fury, plus a select screen.

questions.title: Throws: when should the engine take the victim back?
questions.context: Today the decoded throw script holds the victim only until the throw RELEASES him; then the engine flies him on its own arc. That is where most throws look wrong: the victim's pose pops (head-down to upright in one frame) and his path leaves the source's by up to 51 px. Left = KOF98, right = ours (Terry's back throw). Proposed: the script owns BOTH fighters, position and pose, until the victim LANDS; the engine takes over at the landing. This reverses your 2026-10-08 rule (engine physics as soon as he leaves the hands). The fixes for the screen-edge teleports, the floating victims and the slipping sprites come with it either way.

media.caption: KOF98 (left) vs ours (right), Terry back throw: frames 47 -> 50 = the pose pop, 56-76 = our arc vs KOF's
Hanzo SS2 forward throw: the 92 px teleport at the release near the screen edge

options.label: Script until the landing (recommended): the flight looks like the source
Keep the engine from the release (today), fix only the teleports / floating / sprites
Engine from the release but with the source's speed (overshoots: lands up to 1070 px too far)

sets.title: Krauser: gold questions
sets.intro: Wolfgang Krauser (KOF96), the third fighter golded after Terry and Kim, the heavy one (Haggar). My proposal keeps only the pieces your review kept, and what ships for him today wherever it still fits the new system. Every question: my proposal first, then the alternatives; NONE lets you say your own in the note. Each option plays its moves as small looping clips, left to right; tap a clip for quarter speed, tap a clip in a sequence to replace it with any move (tab 'All animations' = his whole KOF96 table). Specials play whole, as they come out on a hit (projectiles and the victim are not drawn). You can also just answer in chat against the list below.
sets.proposal_title: My whole proposal (what each input does)
proposal: Size: scale 0.91 (his official 200 cm: 110 px next to Terry's 101).
Chain (A A A, 3 hits in all): close C > far D > crouch C, as you chose.
Last hit with the stick: neutral crouch C; forward far C (blows him away); up close D (launches); down crouch D (crumples, plays as a trip); back his throw.

Blitz (free, spammable, not invincible): forward, forward + A = his dash attack (the C+D dropkick, today's); down, down + A = Leg Tomahawk B (236B, the short overhead kick); down, up + A = Blitz Ball (214A, a projectile: free and spammable, like Terry's Power Wave); up, up + A = Kaiser Kick B (623B, the dropkick).

C specials (1 drive chunk, invincible): C = Kaiser Kick D (623D, the long dropkick; also the combo breaker); forward + C = Kaiser Duel Sobat D (41236D, a hop and two kicks); down + C = Leg Tomahawk D (236D, your "dragon move", as today). Light versions free on the Blitz, heavy versions paid on C.
Fury (D) = Kaiser Wave (641236C, today's). MAX (D at low life with the fury ready) = the same Kaiser Wave, stronger.
Air: forward jump + A = jump D; straight jump + A = jump C (both knock down); down + A = jump A (only flinches, hits until he lands).
Holding the enemy: A = close C (today close A, which you called too choppy for a heavy hitter); the throw-out finisher = close D (today's).
His jumping command grab (Kaiser Suplex, 632146 A / C in KOF96: the leaping German suplex): forward / back + C while holding the enemy, in place of his normal throw (a custom move, built later).
Animations to look at: close A (choppy), Leg Tomahawk D (uneven timing), Kaiser Duel Sobat B, jump C, jump CD.
Walk: Haggar's speed (1.54 px a frame, run 2x), already in.
